problem:
The number of particles $N(t)$ in a radioactive substance after $t$ years can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t}=-3N.
$$

If there were $8\,500$ particles initially, calculate the number of particles remaining after $2$ years. Round your answer to the nearest integer.
worked_solution:
We model the number of particles in the substance using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t}=-3N.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
N(t)={N}_{0}\,{e}^{-3t},
$$

where ${N}_{0}$ is the initial value.

We're told that there were $8\,500$ particles initially, so we have ${N}_{0}=8\,500.$

Therefore, the number of particles $N$ at time $t$ is

$$
N(t)=8\,500\,{e}^{-3t}\,.
$$

Finally, to find the number of particles when $t=2,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(2) & =8\,500\,{e}^{-3\cdot 2} \\  & =8\,500\,{e}^{-6} \\  & ≈21.069\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding our answer to the nearest integer, we conclude that $21$ particles remain.
